title: Performance: Thinking Time vs Query Time
brief: Given the uncurated Meridian agent, split a slow answer into thinking time and query
time BEFORE changing anything. The two halves are fixed in completely different places,
and doubling the warehouse fixes neither if the problem is context.
- Measure both halves: system.query.history for the SQL, the Conversation API for
the rest. Instrument your own poll loop as its own span; a naive loop has been
measured adding 6-8 seconds that then get blamed on Genie.
- Write the diagnosis before the fix.
- Apply at least three fixes, each at the correct layer.
- Re-measure and report before and after.
Grading rewards a correct diagnosis over a large speedup. Identifying a thinking-bound
problem and improving it 20% scores higher than doubling the warehouse and getting lucky.
The checks below confirm the agent you are tuning is actually the slow one.
NOTE ON GRADING. The measurement and the diagnosis are what count, and a person reads those. The checks below only confirm you are tuning the right agent.

checks.name: Prerequisite: the uncurated agent exists to tune
checks.hint: Create it with academy.create_agents(). It carries all 14 base objects on purpose.

checks.name: Prerequisite: it still carries the long instruction block
checks.hint: The prose is one of the three things you are measuring the cost of.

checks.name: Prerequisite: it has no example queries yet
checks.hint: Adding them is one of the fixes, not part of the starting state.

review: The diagnosis was written before the fixes, and names which half dominated.
Poll-loop overhead is reported separately from Genie's own time.
Each of the three fixes is at the layer the measurement pointed to.
